records.deidentified_narrative: at the listed date/time police responded to the listed location reference a crash involving a motor vehicle and a pedestrian. upon my arrival assisting officers had secured the scene and ems was on scene treating unit 2 (a pedestrian) who was already inside the ems [medical facility] due to life threatening injuries. i was unable to obtain a statement or identification from unit 2 due to severity of injuries. officer a. hernandez #[medical facility] to advise of any updates with unit 2. i contacted the driver of unit 1. unit 1 driver stated that he was traveling [roadway] traveling around 25-30 miles per hour. unit 1 stated that he did not see unit 2 until it was too late. unit 1 stated that unit 2 was traveling from [roadway]. unit 1 explained that unit 2 was not in the crosswalk and that it was hard to see unit 2 as it was dark and unit 2 was wearing darker clothing. [roadway] north of the crosswalk. unit 1 stated that after he struck unit 2, unit 1 stopped his vehicle and moved unit 2 [roadway]. unit 1 stated that while he was moving unit 2 [roadway] he noticed a strong smell of alcohol coming from unit 2. tid was notified of this case, detective martinez #2407 made the scene and investigated the crash. sgt. laurenz #3366 made the scene. csi angela salvateirra #9415 made the location and processed the scene. officer hernandez #0729 advised me that unit [medical facility] at 2239 hours. i advised tid of the updated information. i then stood by while tid/csi processed the scene. i was advised by the listed detective that the scene could be released. driver of unit 1 was briefed by tid and given follow up information. i collected unit 2 shoes that were left at the scene and i placed them in the property room under barcode number 990001592583.

hernandez, isidro (dob: [date]), hereafter defendant, committed the offense of failure to stop and render aid and driving while intoxicated, in houston, harris county, texas on april 24, 2021. the affiant was in full police uniform and a marked patrol vehicle and was dispatched to [roadway] houston, harris county, texas. this location is a government [roadway] apartments. there are several signs posted throughout the property, stating, ""no loitering, no trespassing, violators will be prosecuted"". deputy josette saldana (86h38), deputy jesus diego (86n11), and deputy ashley thomas (86h22) responded as a back-up unit. deputy made contact with the witness williams, toyce, by obtaining her texas identification card. the witness stated her 14-year-old daughter (t. w.) was struck by a red truck inside a apartment complex, in which i made contact with the juvenile daughter (t. w.) and advised that she felt pain and discomfort from her shoulder. prior from deputies arrival, ems was dispatched and further evaluated the juvenile daughter (t. w.), in which ems advised no bones were broken and if needed and the pain progresses [medical facility]. the witness stated as the red truck was leaving the complex, she attempted to make contact with the driver of the vehicle by screaming and stating, ""you hit my daughter!"" the witness stated that the red truck forward progressed and stayed in motion attempting to exit the property, in which she stayed behind the vehicle and snapped a photo of the rear license plate and further observed the red truck exiting the property onto a public roadway. approximately two hours has lapsed the witness observe the red truck come back inside the property, in which the witness immediately called the police. the witness observed the defendant driving and operating a vehicle, was involved in an accident that resulted in and that was reasonably likely to result of her 14-year-old daughter (t. w.), hereinafter called the complainant, and the defendant intentionally and knowingly failed to immediately stop his vehicle at the scene of the accident and as close to the scene of the accident as possible, failed to immediately return to the scene of said accident, failed to immediately determine whether a person was involved in said accident and determine whether any person at the scene of said accident required aid, and failed to remain at the scene of said accident until the defendant had given the registration number of the vehicle that the defendant was driving to an occupant of the other vehicle involved in said accident made arrangements for [medical facility] for medical treatment after [medical facility]. i conducted a criminal history search inquiry on the defendant and showed that he doesn't have any history in harris county. the witness was able to identify the driver later by personal photo taken from deputy cell phone, in which deputy requested deputy thomas to check by with the witness to confirm the identity. as deputy thomas showed the snapped photo to the witness confirmed the identity of the driver. as the witness can identify the driver by sight. i further identified him to be hernandez, isidro (dob: [date]) by obtaining his us permanent resident card, hereinafter he will be the defendant. the defendant stated that he was inside the apartment complex, but advises that he didn't struck a juvenile upon exiting the complex, in which he was detained for further investigation. as deputy was speaking with the defendant i observed blood shut eyes and strong odor of alcoholic beverage emitting from his person. i asked the defendant if he had alcoholic beverage prior from operating a motor vehicle, at that time, he advised that he had six canned budweiser, in which the last beer he had was at 5:30 pm. deputy diego later informed me that he observed four closed cans cold by the touch budweiser cans, in which the defendant did admit he still had four can left inside his vehicle. i transported the defendant to joint processing center (jpc) to further conduct sfst with a licensed dwi technician. on arrival to jpc, dwi technician daferede (payroll 169302) further conducted the sfst and upon the completion of the test, i deputy alvarado read the dic 24 form in spanish due to the only language the defendant knows. the defendant agreed to give a blood sample, in which it was given at 0056 hours. the results from the sfst's:hgn: lack of smooth pursuit left and right eye, distinct nystagmus @ maximum deviation in the left and right eye. onset vertical nystagmus prior to the 45 degrees: in the left and right eye total of 6 clues. walk and turn: can't keep balance, stepped offline, the wrong number of steps, used arms to balance, missed heel toe and turned improperly total of 6 clues. one leg stand: swayed, used his arms to balance, and placed his foot down multiple times total of 3 clues. i contacted the harris county district attorney's office and spoke to ada baer. deputy explained the facts regarding this case, at which time ada baer accepted two charges of failure to stop and render aid and driving while intoxicated. i declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing happened in harris county, texas, and is true and correct based on information and belief. witness information:williams, toyce mashira - phone # (832) 272-4515

records.public_safe_text: on april 24, 2021, at approximately 2202 hrs. affiant, deputy j. alvarado (86h23), employed with the harris county constables office pct 6 housing division, believes hernandez, isidro (dob: [date]), hereafter defendant, committed the offense of failure to stop and render aid and driving while intoxicated, in houston, harris county, texas on april 24, 2021. the affiant was in full police uniform and a marked patrol vehicle and was dispatched to [roadway] houston, harris county, texas. this location is a government [roadway] apartments. there are several signs posted throughout the property, stating, ""no loitering, no trespassing, violators will be prosecuted"". deputy josette saldana (86h38), deputy jesus diego (86n11), and deputy ashley thomas (86h22) responded as a back-up unit. deputy made contact with the witness williams, toyce, by obtaining her texas identification card. the witness stated her 14-year-old daughter (t. w.) was struck by a red truck inside a apartment complex, in which i made contact with the juvenile daughter (t. w.) and advised that she felt pain and discomfort from her shoulder. prior from deputies arrival, ems was dispatched and further evaluated the juvenile daughter (t. w.), in which ems advised no bones were broken and if needed and the pain progresses [medical facility]. the witness stated as the red truck was leaving the complex, she attempted to make contact with the driver of the vehicle by screaming and stating, ""you hit my daughter!"" the witness stated that the red truck forward progressed and stayed in motion attempting to exit the property, in which she stayed behind the vehicle and snapped a photo of the rear license plate and further observed the red truck exiting the property onto a public roadway. approximately two hours has lapsed the witness observe the red truck come back inside the property, in which the witness immediately called the police. the witness observed the defendant driving and operating a vehicle, was involved in an accident that resulted in and that was reasonably likely to result of her 14-year-old daughter (t. w.), hereinafter called the complainant, and the defendant intentionally and knowingly failed to immediately stop his vehicle at the scene of the accident and as close to the scene of the accident as possible, failed to immediately return to the scene of said accident, failed to immediately determine whether a person was involved in said accident and determine whether any person at the scene of said accident required aid, and failed to remain at the scene of said accident until the defendant had given the registration number of the vehicle that the defendant was driving to an occupant of the other vehicle involved in said accident made arrangements for [medical facility] for medical treatment after [medical facility]. i conducted a criminal history search inquiry on the defendant and showed that he doesn't have any history in harris county. the witness was able to identify the driver later by personal photo taken from deputy cell phone, in which deputy requested deputy thomas to check by with the witness to confirm the identity. as deputy thomas showed the snapped photo to the witness confirmed the identity of the driver. as the witness can identify the driver by sight. i further identified him to be hernandez, isidro (dob: [date]) by obtaining his us permanent resident card, hereinafter he will be the defendant. the defendant stated that he was inside the apartment complex, but advises that he didn't struck a juvenile upon exiting the complex, in which he was detained for further investigation. as deputy was speaking with the defendant i observed blood shut eyes and strong odor of alcoholic beverage emitting from his person. i asked the defendant if he had alcoholic beverage prior from operating a motor vehicle, at that time, he advised that he had six canned budweiser, in which the last beer he had was at 5:30 pm. deputy diego later informed me that he observed four closed cans cold by the touch budweiser cans, in which the defendant did admit he still had four can left inside his vehicle. i transported the defendant to joint processing center (jpc) to further conduct sfst with a licensed dwi technician. on arrival to jpc, dwi technician daferede (payroll 169302) further conducted the sfst and upon the completion of the test, i deputy alvarado read the dic 24 form in spanish due to the only language the defendant knows. the defendant agreed to give a blood sample, in which it was given at 0056 hours. the results from the sfst's:hgn: lack of smooth pursuit left and right eye, distinct nystagmus @ maximum deviation in the left and right eye. onset vertical nystagmus prior to the 45 degrees: in the left and right eye total of 6 clues. walk and turn: can't keep balance, stepped offline, the wrong number of steps, used arms to balance, missed heel toe and turned improperly total of 6 clues. one leg stand: swayed, used his arms to balance, and placed his foot down multiple times total of 3 clues. i contacted the harris county district attorney's office and spoke to ada baer. deputy explained the facts regarding this case, at which time ada baer accepted two charges of failure to stop and render aid and driving while intoxicated. i declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing happened in harris county, texas, and is true and correct based on information and belief. witness information:williams, toyce mashira - phone # (832) 272-4515

records.public_safe_text: unit 2 (pedestrian) was walking across the parking isles perpendicular to the available cross walks. unit 1 (vehicle) was traveling west down the isle to turn south to next isle. driver of unit 1 stated that her passenger alerted her to unit 2 stepping out into the isle and she stopped. pedestrian continued into the front of the vehicle and seemed to notice the car. pedestrian then turned and slammed hands on hood of vehicle and began yelling. subject then began to turn and fell to the ground. unit 1 driver and passenger both advised that the pedestrian hit the vehicle on the hood. i observed two hand prints on the hood/grill area and no other marks in the dust covering the vehicle. ems (pedestrian in ems vehicle when i arrived on scene) advised that the pedestrian stated that she had been walking through the parking lot and observed the vehicle coming toward her and not appearing to stop. ems advised they were told by pedestrian that she turned and put her hands onto the hood and when she turned to continue she fell down. when i spoke to the pedestrian initially she advised me that she had been walking and observed the vehicle coming so she turned and put her hands out to stop it but then was not sure what happened after. after attempting to get video from inside the heb (no manager available but should have video of incident) i was informed by an employee that a passer by had commented about the pedestrian not being hit by the car but falling down as though she was. i spoke to the pedestrian again and this time she was adamant that the car had hit her in her right side but stated that she did not have pain on that side and her only injuries were to her left knee (swollen due to twisting per pedestrian) and a scrape on her left elbow.
